unfold.unfolded: Let $S$ be an ordered semigroup and $m\ge 1$ an integer. A subsemigroup $Q$ of $S$ is an $m$-quasi-ideal of $S$ if $(S^mQ]\cap(QS^m]\subseteq Q$ and $(Q]=Q$, where $(X]=\{x\in S : x\le y \text{ for some } y\in X\}$ and $S^m$ is the set of all products of $m$ elements of $S$.
notes: The closure (X] is not defined in the context; the usual definition is used.

verdict.reason: The unfolded form gives the same conditions on a subsemigroup Q for m≥1. It only makes the notation for the order ideal (X] and the product set S^m explicit.
